source.snippet: We are planning to add MFA to an on-premises Active Directory environment. Our setup is fairly straightforward: Windows Server with on-prem Active Directory, most users authenticate directly against AD, administrators use RDP for server management, part of the infrastructure is isolated from the Internet, so cloud-only MFA services are not an option. We're looking for an MFA approach that can be deployed entirely on-premises while protecting both Windows logons and RDP.

problem_statement: Organizations running air-gapped or internet-restricted on-premises Active Directory environments cannot use cloud-based MFA solutions, yet still need to protect Windows logons and RDP access with multi-factor authentication. Existing on-prem MFA options are complex, expensive, or poorly documented.
target_segment: IT administrators and sysadmins at mid-market companies, government contractors, and regulated-industry firms with on-prem AD and internet-restricted infrastructure
notes: Buyer signal present: this is a business IT context with compliance drivers (regulated industries, government contractors). Companies in this segment routinely pay for security tooling. The air-gapped constraint rules out mainstream SaaS MFA vendors (Duo, Okta, Azure AD), creating a genuine gap. A lightweight on-prem MFA appliance or simplified deployment service/guide could be sold to IT teams. Recurring pain evidenced by the question being asked in 2026 despite MFA being a mature category — the on-prem niche remains underserved.
